attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'it appears' and 'based on every source I can see'. It is a hedged general impression.

contract.note: He gives no threshold for 'years' and does not say whether a data center means one building, a campus or a retrofit. A pass/fail test would need choices he never made.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, introduced with 'I need to be more blunt'.

semantics.note: These are firm present-state claims, and 'vast majority' and 'if they've turned them on at all' are both kept. Dropping the normative clause about disclosure is appropriate.

contract.note: The plain reading (more than half of sold GPUs not installed or powered; most buyers without meaningful revenue) is ordinary. Reading 'warehouses' broadly matches his own wording elsewhere ('warehouses or unpowered data centers'). The window around the post date is reasonable.

evidence.note: One buyer (Amazon) staging GB300 racks without power in August 2026. A single-company anecdote, which the contract treats as context only.
Air Street index compares deployed GPUs with the announced pipeline, not with shipped or sold units. It is also dated just before the window.
NVIDIA 10-Q gives the scale of sales (about $96B for the quarter) but says nothing about what share is installed.

reviews.rationale: No representative source in the packet measures what share of NVIDIA's sold GPUs sat uninstalled around September 2026, or what share of buyers earn meaningful revenue. The Amazon item is one company, Air Street measures announced capacity, and the 10-Q only gives scale. The packet does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'appears' and 'likely' and includes the motive claim. It is a hedged inference about Microsoft's spending and intent.

contract.note: The claim is hedged twice, its motive part cannot be checked, and the dollar size has no disclosed metric to test against. Not scoring it is fair.

evidence.note: Nadella (Nov 2025) said some GPUs were in inventory without power. This fits the direction of the claim but gives no amount, predates the post, and is a company statement.

reviews.rationale: 'It appears' and 'likely' make this a hedged inference, and policy does not score those. The motive ('to hide') cannot be tested. No source gives a value for Microsoft's idle GPUs, and the Nadella remark is only context.
